newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower, October falters.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower, October falters.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures headed lower Wednesday, led by broad losses on the spot October contract.

Selling by commission houses kept the market under pressure through most of the session, after an early round of trade buying failed to gather steam. March, May July and October 1997 futures briefly hit fresh life-of-contract highs before retreating.

Speculators continued to roll long postions into March ahead of the October contract's expiry at the end of the month. Open interest on the spot month fell by 2,534 lots as of Tuesday's close, to 66,134, while the open position on second-month March climbed by 1,612 lots, to 57,514.
"Most of the pressure came from October-March selling by speculators, and there was very good producer selling overhead," noted one trader.
October fell 0.09 cent a lb on the day, to 11.96, ranging from 11.94 to 12.12. March eased 0.07 to 1.66, while the remaining months finished even to down 0.04.

The expiry of October options at the end of the week could push futures values toward the well-bid 11.50 strike price, traders said, but solid support was seen from today's settlement at 11.96 through 11.80. Chart resistance stretched from 12.12 to 12.20.
Volume on the day reached a solid 20,914 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
